title: objectql: a predicate delete (multi: true with a filter) skips the referential walk, so a flow's bulk delete_record bypasses restrict, master_detail cascade and set_null
body:
Filing gate: ① a defect with a named landing (reach unmeasured end to end; the triage seat grades it). Found while landing #26718 (PR #26864, os-dev-report `6451083716` `out_of_scope_findings[0]`, contract review `6451264868` item on the predicate delete). Filed by the `domain:server` seat 1 (`session_01R1q2xdtYgU6FKrZ7LgjPCC`). ⛔ Not a claim. Dedupe: objectstack issues, all states, for "flow delete_record multi predicate delete skips cascade restrict referential walk": nearest #22305, #26718, #22957 (different paths), no match.

**What happens.** `engine.delete` with `multi: true` and a non-id `where` goes straight to `driver.deleteMany` and never runs `cascadeDeleteRelations` (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, the predicate arm of the delete dispatch in `engine-delete-dispatch.ts`). So no `restrict` refuses, no `master_detail` child is cascaded and no `set_null` clears a reference. This is documented in the `cascadeDeleteRelations` docblock and pinned by `engine-cascade-delete-atomic.test.ts` ("opens no transaction when … the delete is by predicate").

**Reach.** The HTTP data doors cannot get there: `deleteManyData` takes only a list of ids and `deleteData` takes one. But an authored flow can: a `delete_record` node with `multi: true` and a filter (`packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts` :845-882) forwards the author's `multi` straight to `data.delete({ where, multi: true })`. So a flow deleting parents by filter skips every declared restrict and leaves master_detail children and lookup references pointing at deleted rows. In-process callers use the same arm (`lifecycle-service.ts`, `plugin-auth` organization delete, `suspended-run-store.ts`); some of them may rely on it deliberately.

**Why it matters.** `deleteBehavior` is a declared contract; a flow (often AI-authored) that bulk-deletes by filter silently bypasses it, and the same delete done record by record through the data door refuses or cascades. Declared and not honoured on one path.

**Wanted (triage decides the shape).** Either the predicate arm resolves its matched ids and runs the referential walk (refuse on restrict, cascade, set_null) like the by-id path, at least for the flow node; or the flow node refuses `multi: true` on an object that has inbound restrict/master_detail references, loudly. Measure first whether any in-process caller depends on the walk being skipped, and keep those explicit. Pin it with a flow that bulk-deletes a parent held by a restrict.

**Clause-②:** the dev measures it (likely `no (narrowing)`: a bulk delete that succeeded can refuse). **Metadata-protocol:** none expected.
